mechanism: Withdrawal of Roman authority from Britain left a power vacuum that Anglo-Saxon groups filled with small kingdoms such as Wessex.
The Magyar defeat at Lechfeld in 955 ended their raids and pushed them toward settlement and Christianization under Stephen.
Saladin, a Zengid officer, seized Egypt in 1171 and built the Ayyubid state out of Zengid Syria and Egypt.
Crusader states prompted Saladin's campaigns to unify Muslim Syria and Egypt against the Franks.
Saladin's army annihilated the Crusader force at Hattin, opening the way for the Ayyubids to take Jerusalem.
Saladin's 1187 recapture of Jerusalem provoked the Third Crusade.
After the Ayyubid collapse in Egypt, its Mamluk military officers seized power and founded the Mamluk Sultanate in 1250.
Collapse of Turkic khaganate authority in the Pontic-Caspian steppe let Bulgar groups form independent polities.
Norman conquest of southern Italy and Sicily created the Norman royal state that became the Kingdom of Sicily in 1130.
The 1282 Sicilian Vespers split the realm, leaving the mainland as the Kingdom of Naples under Angevin rule.
Spanish American wars of independence removed Spanish rule from northern South America, creating the space for Gran Colombia's founding.
Bolivar's 1819 victory at Boyaca secured New Granada, enabling the Congress of Cucuta to proclaim Gran Colombia.
The Byzantine defeat at Manzikert in 1071 opened Anatolia to Seljuk Turkish rule, enabling the Sultanate of Rum.
Seljuk control of Anatolia and Nicaea prompted Byzantine appeals to the West that helped launch the First Crusade.
After the Sultanate of Rum fragmented in 1307, its successor Turkish beyliks, including the Ottomans, emerged in Anatolia.
The 2014 annexation and the Donbas uprising that followed opened the wider Russo-Ukrainian war, fought from 2014 onward.
Fighting in eastern Ukraine after the annexation produced the Minsk ceasefire negotiations and protocol of 2014.
Public anxiety over the surge of migrants fueled the Leave campaign and the 2016 referendum that led to Brexit.
Yugoslavia's breakup and Serbian nationalism left Kosovo's Albanian majority under Belgrade's rule, fueling armed secessionist conflict.
Richard I's conquest of Cyprus during the Third Crusade led to its sale to the Templars and the later Lusignan kingdom.
Nazi Germany's 1941 invasion of the USSR sent Army Group North to Leningrad, starting the siege.
The devastation of the Second World War drove Western European states toward economic integration, leading to the Treaty of Rome.
The Treaty of Rome's European Economic Community was transformed into the European Union by the 1992 Maastricht Treaty.
The Second Sino-Japanese War brought Japanese armies to Nanjing after the Battle of Shanghai, where atrocities followed its fall.
Reformation and Counter-Reformation religious conflict shaped the anxious, unstable style of Mannerist art.
Industrialization transformed Britain's economy, cities and class structure, defining the social and economic character of the Victorian era.
Tokugawa Ieyasu's victory at Sekigahara in 1600 gave him the dominance that led to his founding of the Tokugawa shogunate in 1603.
The Sengoku civil wars produced the military unification that Tokugawa Ieyasu inherited and formalized as the shogunate.
Tokugawa shogunate policies restricted foreign contact and trade, producing the sakoku system of national isolation.
Tokugawa persecution of Christians and heavy taxation in Shimabara provoked the 1637-1638 uprising.
The Congress of Vienna restored conservative monarchies and suppressed national aspirations, fueling the liberal and nationalist revolts of 1848.
Urbanization and economic distress from industrialization produced a restive urban working class that joined the 1848 revolts.
The 1848 revolts drew Piedmont into the First Italian War of Independence, a step on the road to a unified Kingdom of Italy.
The 1958 crisis over Algeria brought de Gaulle back to power and the constitution of the Fifth Republic, which created the office of prime minister.
The Ottoman-Venetian war over Cyprus prompted the Holy League that assembled the fleet which fought at Lepanto.
The French Revolution overthrew the monarchy, and the National Convention proclaimed the republic in September 1792.
Austrian and Prussian invasion threats in 1792 radicalized revolutionary politics and hardened the move to a republic.
French armies overthrew the Dutch Republic in 1795 and imposed the Batavian Republic as a client state.
French military intervention in Switzerland in 1798 imposed the Helvetic Republic as a dependent client state.
Instability under the Directory let Napoleon seize power in the 18 Brumaire coup of 1799, ending the republican regime.
Louis IX's defeat in Egypt during the Seventh Crusade let Mamluk commanders consolidate power, which they seized in 1250.
The Mamluk victory at Ain Jalut in 1260 halted the Mongol advance into Egypt and Syria.
Mamluk decline and internal rivalry in the early 1500s left Syria and Egypt open to Ottoman conquest in 1516-1517.
The division of the Roman Empire into eastern and western halves let the eastern church develop into the Orthodox tradition.
Nazi atrocities of the Holocaust motivated the postwar push to codify human rights in binding international covenants.
Germany's colonial push under Bismarck led him to summon the 1884-1885 conference that set the rules for partitioning Africa.
Ottoman control of eastern trade routes after 1453 motivated Iberian searches for a westward sea route to Asia.
Tokugawa Ieyasu's victory at Sekigahara in 1600 established the hegemony from which the Edo period began in 1603.
The prosperous merchant culture of Edo sustained the ukiyo-e woodblock print tradition.
The Christian Reconquista of the Iberian Peninsula created the frontier kingdom of Aragon in the Pyrenees.
The 1479 dynastic union of Aragon and Castile under Ferdinand and Isabella laid the basis for the Spanish monarchy and empire.
Alfonso V of Aragon took Naples in 1442, bringing the kingdom under Aragonese rule.
The Congo Crisis of 1960-1966 produced the instability in which Mobutu seized power and built the Zaire state.
Zaire's decayed state, unable to control its eastern provinces, provoked the 1996-1997 rebellion known as the First Congo War.
The Battle of Plassey gave the British East India Company political control in Bengal, an early step in the colonial rule that nationalism later resisted.
